name: Arroz con Carne Molida (Mexican Beef and Rice Skillet)
intro_html: This is the Mexican beef and rice skillet your grocery budget has been waiting for: seasoned ground beef, rice, corn, and tomatoes with green chilies, all buried under melted cheese. Each bowl brings {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories for about ${{cost_ps}} (at everyday cost). One skillet, one spoon, fourteen dinners.
ingredients_display: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2.3 cans (1008 g)
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 2.3 cans (660 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rice, 5.25 cups dry: ~$1.18. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 2.3 cans: ~$1.91. Buy 3 cans: $2.46.
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies, 2.3 cans: ~$2.03. Buy 3 10oz cans: $2.61.
Mexican Cheese Blend, 28 oz: ~$6.03. Buy 4 8 oz bags: $6.90.
Pantry seasonings (taco seasoning, salt, black pepper): ~$0.46. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $34.44 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.46 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $41.44 across 14 servings, roughly $2.96 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $4.57 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $46.01. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a plate that would run you triple at any Tex-Mex joint, and you get to keep the leftover chips money.
shop_smart:
The 93/7 ground beef is the biggest line item. Watch for the big club-size packs, which run cheaper per pound, and stock the freezer when it dips.
Store-brand diced tomatoes with green chilies taste the same as the name brand Ro-Tel and usually cost 20 to 30 percent less. Check the price per ounce tag and let math decide.
Shredded cheese goes on sale constantly. Buy the 8 oz bags when they hit a real markdown and freeze what you do not use; it melts fine after thawing.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Brown the ground beef in your largest skillet or pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up as it cooks, until no pink remains (ground beef should hit 160F). Drain excess fat.
Stir in the taco seasoning, diced onion, minced jalapeno, and garlic. Cook 3 to 4 minutes until the onion softens.
Add the dry rice and stir for 1 to 2 minutes so it toasts lightly in the beef drippings.

Pour in the diced tomatoes with green chilies, the corn with its liquid, and enough water to cook the rice (about 2 cups of water per cup of dry rice, minus the can liquid). Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a boil, then cover and reduce to a low simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed. Stir once halfway so nothing sticks.
Kill the heat, scatter the Mexican cheese blend over the top, and cover for 3 to 4 minutes until it melts into the rice.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each of 14 containers and you have identical dinners all week. Every bowl comes in at {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

recipeIngredient: Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 2.3 cans (1008 g)
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies, 2.3 cans (660 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large pot until no pink remains, then drain.
Add taco seasoning, onion, jalapeno, and garlic and cook until softened.
Toast the dry rice in the beef drippings for 1 to 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes with green chilies, corn, and water, then simmer covered 18 to 20 minutes.
Top with Mexican cheese blend, cover until melted, and portion into 14 containers.
